additionalInfo.title: Additional Information about AQI
additionalInfo.definition: The Air Quality Index (AQI) is a measurement used to assess air pollution levels and their impact on human health.
additionalInfo.calculation: AQI is calculated based on 6 main pollutants: PM2.5, PM10, O₃, NO₂, SO₂ and CO. The AQI ranges from 0 to 500, with higher values indicating greater pollution levels.
additionalInfo.dataSource: Data is updated in real-time from city environmental monitoring stations and reliable international data sources.

pollutants.title: Main Pollutants
pollutants.pm25Desc: Fine particulate matter with diameter ≤ 2.5 micrometers, dangerous as it can penetrate deep into lungs.
pollutants.pm10Desc: Particulate matter with diameter ≤ 10 micrometers, causes respiratory irritation.
pollutants.o3Desc: Ground-level ozone, causes lung and respiratory irritation.
pollutants.no2Desc: Nitrogen dioxide from vehicle emissions, causes respiratory inflammation.
pollutants.so2Desc: Sulfur dioxide from burning fossil fuels.
pollutants.coDesc: Carbon monoxide, colorless and odorless gas, dangerous at high concentrations.

health.title: Health Recommendations
health.sensitiveNote: (People with heart/lung disease, asthma, pregnant women)
health.preventiveTip1: Wear dust masks when going outside (N95, N99)
health.preventiveTip3: Close windows when air quality is poor
health.preventiveTip4: Wash hands, eyes, and nose regularly
health.preventiveTip5: Drink plenty of water, eat vegetables and fruits
health.avoidTip1: Outdoor exercise when air quality is poor
health.avoidTip2: Prolonged exposure of children and elderly to polluted air
health.avoidTip4: Burning trash or fires that contribute to air pollution
health.avoidTip5: Smoking and exposure to cigarette smoke
health.emergencyMessage: Air quality is at hazardous levels. If you experience difficulty breathing, chest pain, or other abnormal symptoms, contact immediately:

sunProtection.title: Sun Protection Recommendations
sunProtection.tip1: Use SPF 30+ sunscreen when going outside
sunProtection.tip2: Wear a hat and sunglasses to protect skin and eyes
sunProtection.tip3: Limit outdoor activities from 11am-3pm when UV index is high
sunProtection.tip4: Drink enough water to avoid dehydration on hot days

rainProtection.title: Rain Protection Recommendations
rainProtection.tip1: Bring a raincoat or umbrella when going outside
rainProtection.tip2: Check weather forecast before traveling far
rainProtection.tip3: Avoid deep flooded areas and fast-flowing water
rainProtection.tip4: Drive slowly and carefully when it rains
rainProtection.tip5: Stay away from power poles and electrical wires during thunderstorms
